rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the baseline performance of RNA-only modeling with PCA encoding. It clarifies whether RNA-only models can achieve competitive accuracy and isolates the impact of the RNA encoder choice (pca_n2000) before exploring more complex multimodal configurations. This is the best first step to establish a baseline and understand the importance of RNA representation.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the impact of profile setting and aggregation. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether multiprofile or aggregation improves performance, which are critical design choices. This balances exploration of key factors while building on the baseline.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002, 0.59 accuracy) outperform singleprofile (config_001, 0.48). This experiment tests whether switching RNA encoders from pca_n2000 (config_002) to scvi_n200 while keeping multiprofile and avgpool aggregation (key factors in config_002's success) isolates the impact of encoder choice. This clarifies if encoder architecture is a critical design decision, balancing exploration of RNA representation improvements with exploitation of multiprofile's proven benefit.

Existing evidence shows that for rna_only multiprofile models, scvi_n200 (0.65 accuracy) outperforms pca_n2000 (0.59 accuracy). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (used in config_005) with transformer aggregation (config_006) further improves performance for scvi_n200. It isolates the effect of aggregation method while maintaining the proven RNA encoder and profile setting, directly addressing whether transformer's capacity for sequential modeling provides additional value.

Existing evidence shows RNA-only multiprofile models with scvi_n200 encoder and avgpool aggregation achieve high accuracy (0.652970). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to scgpt (a more complex model) in the same multiprofile setup isolates the impact of representation choice. It directly compares two key design decisions (encoder type) while keeping other factors constant, reducing uncertainty about which RNA encoder is more effective.

Existing evidence shows scvi_n200 (RNA encoder) and avgpool (aggregation) are effective in rna_only setups (config_005/006). This experiment tests whether combining these with multimodal data (resnet50 image encoder) improves performance, isolating the effect of adding image modality. It balances exploitation (using proven components) and exploration (testing multimodal integration), addressing key uncertainty about whether multimodal models can outperform rna_only.

Existing evidence shows that rna_only models with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation (config_006) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6529). This experiment tests whether combining this top rna_only configuration with image data (resnet50 encoder) using the same transformer aggregation and concat fusion (a logical extension) can improve performance. It isolates the effect of adding multimodal data to the best rna-only setup, addressing uncertainty about whether multimodal approaches can surpass unimodal performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (config_033) achieve high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with the more powerful imagenet_vit_l image encoder while using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. It isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical component, and evaluates whether the stronger encoder compensates for the simpler aggregation method, providing insight into which design choice (encoder or aggregation) has greater influence on performance.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_033) achieve high validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether using the imagenet_vit_l image encoder (instead of resnet50) maintains this performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice. It is a logical extension of the high-performing config_033, isolating the effect of the image encoder while keeping other critical components (RNA encoder, aggregation, fusion) consistent.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_039) achieve high validation accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt (while keeping other components identical) improves performance, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing setup with exploration of a key design decision (RNA encoder) that may influence results.
